title: SGD at the Edge of Stability: The Stochastic Sharpness Gap
claim: Smaller mini-batches settle at systematically lower equilibrium sharpness than full-batch training, a pattern that holds across architectures.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, shared legend style, dashed GD curve and dotted 2/η threshold
description: Two side-by-side line plots labeled A and B. Both show sharpness (largest Hessian eigenvalue) on the y-axis against training step (0 to 20k) on the x-axis. Each has curves for batch sizes b=50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000, colored from dark purple through magenta and orange to yellow. A dashed dark-gray curve shows full-batch GD, and a dotted horizontal line marks 2/η = 200. Shaded bands show variation across seeds. In panel A, sharpness dips, rises quickly, then plateaus. Large batches and GD sit at or just above 200, while b=50 plateaus near 190. In panel B, sharpness rises more gradually. Large batches reach about 200, while b=50 stays far lower, around 130. A legend sits at the lower right of each panel. The eye goes first to the fanned-out curves below the dotted threshold line.
caption: Sharpness $\lambda_{\max}(\nabla^2 L)$ during training for different batch sizes. (A) FC-Tanh + MSE: smaller batch sizes produce markedly lower equilibrium sharpness. The dashed black curve shows full-batch GD. (B) CNN + MSE: the same pattern holds with a convolutional architecture, with an even larger gap ($S_{\mathrm{eq}} \approx 131$ at $b=50$ vs.\ $S_{\mathrm{GD}} \approx 202$). Shaded regions indicate $\pm 1$ standard deviation across 5 seeds.
abstract: When training neural networks with full-batch gradient descent (GD) and step size $Î·$, the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian -- the sharpness $S(\boldsymbolÎ¸)$ -- rises to $2/Î·$ and hovers there, a phenomenon termed the Edge of Stability (EoS). \citet{damian2023selfstab} showed that this behavior is explained by a self-stabilization mechanism driven by third-order structure of the loss, and that GD implicitly follows projected gradient descent (PGD) on the constraint $ S(\boldsymbolÎ¸)\leq 2/Î·$. For mini-batch stochastic gradient descent (SGD), the sharpness stabilizes below $2/Î·$, with the gap widening as the batch size decreases; yet no theoretical explanation exists for this suppression. We introduce stochastic self-stabilization, extending the self-stabilization framework to SGD. Our key insight is that gradient noise injects variance into the oscillatory dynamics along the top Hessian eigenvector, strengthening the cubic sharpness-reducing force and shifting the equilibrium below $2/Î·$. Following the approach of \citet{damian2023selfstab}, we define stochastic predicted dynamics relative to a moving projected gradient descent trajectory and prove a stochastic coupling theorem that bounds the deviation of SGD from these predictions. We derive a closed-form equilibrium sharpness gap: $ÎS = Î·Î²Ï_{\boldsymbol{u}}^{2}/(4Î±)$, where $Î±$ is the progressive sharpening rate, $Î²$ is the self-stabilization strength, and $Ï_{ \boldsymbol{u}}^{2}$ is the gradient noise variance projected onto the top eigenvector. This formula predicts that smaller batch sizes yield flatter solutions and recovers GD when the batch equals the full dataset.
